lines.text: Each camera can send up to fifty photos a second. Every photo puts the tag in a slightly different place.
In our simulator, far photos scatter by a couple of centimeters, and close photos by a couple of millimeters.
If two friends guessed where a door is, you'd trust the one standing next to it. Same idea here.
So the robot keeps one best guess and nudges it toward each new photo: a big nudge for a sharp photo, a small one for a fuzzy one.
As photos agree, the guess gets surer, and each new photo moves it less. It's a smart average.
A photo more than twenty five centimeters from the guess is ignored. After three jumps in a row, the robot decides it was wrong, and starts over.
Some photos are unsure. Seen straight on, a tag can look tilted either way. Those photos are skipped.
Three good photos, and the robot is locked on. Now its goal comes from the tag.
In the last few centimeters, the tag leaves the cameras' view. Its place in the wheel world is known, so the wheels finish the job.
